_comment: Authoritative pinned commits for every real-world benchmark codebase.
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Consumed by both:
- playbooks/setup-benchmark-repos.yml  (provisioning: clone + checkout)
- python -m bench corpus-check         (verification: still at the pin?)
Do not duplicate these SHAs anywhere else. Each is the commit its
ground-truth oracle was adjudicated against, so changing one silently
invalidates every ground_truth row for that project (the oracle is keyed
on project+commit+file+line+rule). Re-pin only alongside a re-adjudication.
'name' is also the checkout directory basename and the CODEBASES registry
key in bench/realworld_runner.py -- bench/db.py's result-filename
parsing requires all three to match, which is why pure-ftpd is checked out
as 'pureftpd' (no hyphen).
'scope_include'/'scope_exclude': the machine-readable form of
each project's precision_audit/<project>/README.md '## Scope' section --
fnmatch glob lists matched against the project-relative path bench/db.py
already normalizes findings to (project_relpath()). No 'scope_include' key
means unrestricted (whole-repo audit: libcrc only). Include is a
whitelist; exclude further narrows it. 'bench realworld-unlabeled' applies
this by default (see bench/corpus.py:in_scope); pass --no-scope to opt out.
Re-derive from the README, don't hand-edit ad hoc -- these two must stay
in sync (the README is the human-readable rationale, this is what code runs).
'primary_build_config' (ADR-0010 Decision 6): the ONE build
configuration each corpus's precision/recall figure is a statement about.
It was implicit until now -- Linux/POSIX on the benchmark host for every
corpus except ventoy, which is a Win32 program measured as the suite's
Win32 oracle. Declaring it is what makes 'this only compiles under X' a
SCOPE question with an answer instead of an argument.
It is a DECLARATION, not a filter. Nothing reads it to drop findings, and
adding it changed no score: 'out_of_config' paths are still scanned, still
labeled as written (ADR-0010 Decision 1), and still in the denominator.
Narrowing scope_exclude to match it would invalidate thousands of existing
ground_truth rows and is Brandon's call, not a mechanical follow-up.
out_of_config        in-scope paths this configuration never compiles.
out_of_config_state  'clean' = scope and configuration agree;
'scored' = out_of_config paths carry labeled rows
today, i.e. an open denominator gap.
WHAT THE FIELD CANNOT SAY. It is path-granular, so it expresses a file the
build never compiles and NOT an #ifdef arm inside a file the build does
compile (hostap's WORDS_BIGENDIAN arm, sqlite's #if SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED>30).
Those stay in the denominator with no way to mark them; 'endianness' and
'arch' are declared so an adjudicator can at least name the axis.
The boundary is PLATFORM and ARCHITECTURE only. A feature or debug flag
inside the primary configuration's build (CONFIG_SAE, NDEBUG,
CONFIG_TESTING_OPTIONS) is NOT a scope boundary -- those findings are
labeled on the construct alone (ADR-0010 Decision 1, and the ~195 hostap
DCL13-C TPs in CONFIG_* #else stubs are correct under it).
GLOB SEMANTICS ARE PATH-AWARE: '*' and '?' and '[...]' stop at '/', and
'**' is what crosses one. So 'src/**' means everything under src/ at any
depth, 'src/*.c' means only the .c files directly in src/, and the two
are NOT the same thing.
This paragraph used to say the opposite -- that these were fnmatch
patterns where '*' crosses '/' -- and that was true when the predicate
first inherited fnmatch's semantics. benchmarking_db's bench_db/corpus.py
replaced it: fnmatch has no concept of a path, so '*.c' also matched
testes/libs/lib1.c and handed lua five files sqc never scans, overstating
its coverage denominator by 8%. The new predicate was applied to all nine
pinned (project, commit) pairs before the change: eight return a
byte-identical file set and lua drops exactly those five. Nothing was
audited under testes/, so that is a denominator correction only.
raylib is the entry worth naming, because it looks like a break and is
not. It declares 'src/external/*' as an exclude, which under fnmatch was
load-bearing: 'src/*.c' reached into src/external/glfw/... and the exclude
pulled it back out, 121 files -> 23. Under path-aware matching 'src/*.c'
never reaches there, so the exclude is now a no-op -- and the answer is 23
either way. Same set, reached honestly. Keep the exclude regardless: it
still states the intent, and it is what makes the two semantics agree.
A NEW declaration that means 'recursively' must therefore write '**'. One
that writes '*' and means it gets the narrower answer, which is usually
what you want -- and benchmarking_db's assertions check both directions of
drift between what these globs accept and what the runner actually
scans.

primary_build_config.summary: Portable C with no platform-alternative sources; the whole audit scope compiles here.
Default autoconf build, SQLITE_OS_UNIX. Compile-time limits at their defaults (SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED=10).
Default Linux broker + libmosquitto build (epoll mux, no WITH_WEBSOCKETS_BUILTIN change).
Linux/OpenSSL build. The 14 Windows/Apple WIN_MAC files are already in scope_exclude; out_of_config lists two more that are not.
wpa_supplicant + hostapd at their shipped defconfigs: CONFIG_DRIVER_NL80211/WEXT/WIRED/MACSEC_LINUX, os_unix, l2_packet_linux.
Default `make linux` build (LUA_USE_LINUX). Platform variation is intra-file in luaconf.h, not per-file.
PLATFORM_DESKTOP_GLFW. rcore.c #includes exactly one platforms/*.c as source, so the other nine are never compiled.
Default configure build. The bsd-*.c portability fallbacks are unconditional in src/Makefile.am, so they are in-configuration.
KernelPlatform=pc99 KernelArch=x86, the compile_commands.json configuration. CMake selects one arch/ and one plat/ subtree; the rest are never compiled.
Default mbedtls_config.h. Every library/*.c is compiled; feature gating is intra-file and is not a scope boundary.
Default Linux server build; no platform-alternative sources in scope.
Ventoy2Disk is a Win32 GUI installer: this corpus is the suite's Win32 oracle, scanned on the Linux host but measuring Windows code. Not a Linux configuration.
